newsitem.title: USA: Genzyme down after Cowen lowers '97 EPS.
newsitem.headline: Genzyme down after Cowen lowers '97 EPS.

text.p: Genzyme Corp's stock price was down more than two points in mid-afternoon trading Monday after Cowen & Co lowered its 1997 earnings estimate for the biotechnology company to $1.20 per share from $1.40.

"The only thing that I have seen that could account for the drop is that Cowen has reduced its earnings per share for 1997," Genzyme Chief Financial Officer David McLachlan said in a telephone interview.
Cowen analyst David Stone, who follows Cambridge, Mass.-based Genzyme, was not available for comment.
McLachlan said the stock had risen 25 percent since the November Thanksgiving Day holiday. "It's been trading very strongly in just the last couple of weeks and has gone from $20 to $25.
"The stock's been very strong and perhaps this was the signal the Street needed."
The Wall Street consensus on Genzyme's 1997 earnings is $1.30 a share, McLachlan said.
